record.paper_title: Relativistic jets in narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies. New discoveries and open questions
record.original_question: Is there a limiting black-hole mass above which active galactic nuclei are preferentially radio-loud, and if so how does that threshold apply to narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies whose commonly quoted black-hole masses are lower than those of typical radio-loud quasars?

evidence.quote: Is there a limiting BH mass above which objects are preferentially radio-loud?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Active galactic nuclei (AGN) are commonly classified as "radio-loud" or "radio-quiet" according to the ratio R = F_{5 GHz}/F_{B} of the radio flux density at 5 GHz to the optical B-band flux density, with R > 10 conventionally defining radio-loud sources. Among AGN, narrow-line Seyfert 1 (NLS1) galaxies form a subclass characterized by relatively narrow permitted optical emission lines (FWHM(Hβ) < 2000 km/s), strong Fe II emission, and a weak [O III]/Hβ ratio; their inferred central black-hole masses are typically in the range 10^6–10^8 M_⊙, lower than the masses 10^8–10^9 M_⊙ usually attributed to radio-loud quasars and radio galaxies.

Address the following questions quantitatively, on the basis of the observed populations of AGN:

(a) Does there exist a threshold black-hole mass M_BH^{crit} such that AGN with M_BH > M_BH^{crit} are preferentially radio-loud (in the sense that the radio-loud fraction increases sharply above this threshold), and if so determine M_BH^{crit}.

(b) Given the existence of radio-loud NLS1 galaxies whose commonly quoted black-hole masses lie well below M_BH^{crit}, reconcile this with the threshold of part (a): either (i) demonstrate that the standard mass estimators (e.g., based on the broad-line region radius–luminosity relation and the virial formula M_BH ∝ R_{BLR} v^2/G with v inferred from FWHM(Hβ)) systematically underestimate M_BH in NLS1s by a factor sufficient to place them above M_BH^{crit}, or (ii) show that radio loudness in NLS1s arises from a physical mechanism that does not require M_BH > M_BH^{crit} (for example, dependence on spin, accretion rate in Eddington units, or jet-launching conditions distinct from those of classical radio-loud quasars).
artifact.status_search_result: The relationship between black-hole mass and radio loudness in AGN, especially the existence of radio-loud narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies, remains an actively debated open problem in extragalactic astrophysics. Although Fermi/LAT detections of γ-ray emitting NLS1s have shown that relativistic jets can be launched from systems with apparently low black-hole masses, no consensus threshold M_BH has been established, and proposed resolutions (mass underestimation due to disk inclination, high spin, super-Eddington accretion, etc.) are still under investigation.

status_evidence.title: Relativistic jets in narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies
status_evidence.snippet: Open questions are listed including whether there is a limiting BH mass above which objects are preferentially radio-loud.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an open question in the field.
